extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy analysts, and patent analysts using multi-indicator frameworks to assess patent quality (cross-national, firm- and industry-level analyses)
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalizing patent quality using the OECD multi-indicator framework: bibliometric, family/renewal, examination-based indicators, cohort normalization, and composite scoring for cross-national/industry/firm comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward Citations (5-year window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of times the patent is cited by subsequent patents within 5 years of grant. Normalized by technology field and year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 5-year post-grant citation window and cohort-normalize (by technology field and grant year). High forward-citation counts (top quartile within cohort) are interpreted as high technological impact/value; low counts indicate low impact. Beware citation lags and field differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality Index
rubrics_metrics.description: Captures breadth of technology fields the patent draws on. Computed as 1 - Σ(share of backward citations in each IPC class)² (Trajtenberg, Henderson & Jaffe 1997).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher values indicate the patent draws on a more diverse set of technological fields (more original). Cohort- and field-normalize when comparing across technologies. Originality should be interpreted alongside other indicators (e.g., generality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality Index
rubrics_metrics.description: Captures breadth of technology fields the patent influences. Computed as 1 - Σ(share of forward citations in each IPC class)².
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher values indicate the patent influences a more diverse set of technological fields (more general). Use cohort/field normalization; high generality combined with high originality signals cross-cutting inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radicalness Index
rubrics_metrics.description: Time-invariant count of IPC classes that the patent's backward citations are in but that the patent itself is not classified in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher counts indicate the patent draws from foreign technological domains and is more 'radical'. This metric is structural (time-invariant) and complements originality/generality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Scope (IPC classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of distinct IPC sub-classes assigned to the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater number of IPC subclasses suggests broader claimed scope. Use with claim-count metrics and normalization by technology area to infer breadth of technical coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Size
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patent offices where the patent family is filed (geographic coverage of filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger families signal greater applicant belief in commercial value; triadic families (US + EP + JP) are treated as the strongest signal. Beware that applicant strategy, market targets, and cost constraints affect family size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of years maintenance fees are paid before lapse (renewal duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents renewed to full term (e.g., 20 years) signal high commercial value; early abandonment or lapse at first maintenance fee signals lower commercial significance. Renewal patterns vary by jurisdiction and applicant strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Lag
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long grant lag may indicate disputed patentability or strategic delay; short grant lag may indicate weak examination or clearly patentable inventions. Interpret grant lag with caution—jurisdictional procedures and applicant prosecution strategies influence it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of inventors listed on the patent document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger inventor teams correlate with more substantial inventions and R&D investment. Use as a proxy for collaborative intensity; adjust for field norms (some fields commonly have larger teams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Backward Citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of prior patents and literature cited by the patent (backward citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More backward citations may signal a deeper technological lineage or more thorough prior-art search; few citations could indicate pioneering work or weak prior-art disclosure. Practices for citation vary by office/examiner and over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Count and Independent Claim Count
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of claims and number of independent claims in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher claim counts and more independent claims can signal a broader scope strategy. Combine with IPC-based scope metrics and examination outcomes to assess asserted breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Score (OECD aggregate index)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate quality score constructed by weighting multiple indicators (technological and economic) and cohort-normalizing by technology field and year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple indicators (not just citations) and normalize within cohorts for comparability. The composite allows classification into high/medium/low quality within technology fields and years. The weighting scheme matters—report weights and sensitivity analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Quality Composite (operational marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination of high-performing indicator values that together indicate strong patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OECD operative definition of 'strong' includes: forward citations top-quartile (within cohort); triadic family; originality and generality both top-quartile; renewed to full term; multiple inventor team. Meeting these conditions places a patent among highest-quality grants in its cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak Quality Composite (operational marker)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combination of low-performing indicator values that together indicate weak patent quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OECD operative definition of 'weak' includes: forward citations bottom-quartile; US-only family; originality and generality both bottom-quartile; abandoned at first maintenance fee; single inventor. These signal low commercial/technological significance within cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort-normalization and field/year controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons must be cohort-normalized by technology field and grant (or application) year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize each indicator within technology-year cohorts to account for citation practices, grant timing, and field-specific dynamics. Cross-industry or cross-jurisdiction comparisons require careful normalization and sensitivity checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum post-grant observation window (measurement horizon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement requires sufficient post-grant time (recommended 5+ years) for indicators like forward citations to stabilize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many OECD indicators rely on post-grant observation (e.g., 5-year forward citation window). Do not evaluate recent patents using citation-based indicators; consider alternative short-term proxies or wait for the observation window to elapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and interpretation caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators are correlated and no single indicator is sufficient; strategic patenting and industry differences can confound interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize correlated signals (e.g., family size and renewals) and that strategic uses (defensive, blocking filings) can inflate some indicators without reflecting quality. Perform industry-specific normalization and interpret composites with awareness of these confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative Five-Test Checklist (practical evaluation procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical test for assessing issued patents (5+ years post-grant): 1) Forward citations vs. cohort: top quartile? 2) Originality and generality: both top quartile? 3) Family size: triadic? 4) Renewal status: paid through current period? 5) Aggregate into composite score and classify as high/medium/low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as a pragmatic screening tool; a patent passing all five tests is among the highest-quality grants in its cohort. Document cohort definitions, windows, and thresholds used (e.g., quartiles).
